five_minute_explanation: One participant is the Game Master, who presents the world and decides which parts of the GURPS toolkit are active.
Each other participant controls one point-built character rather than choosing a mandatory class and level.
Most uncertain tasks use 3d6: roll at or below effective skill or attribute.
In combat, choose a maneuver each one-second turn. A successful attack normally still allows the target an active defense.
If the defense fails, roll damage, subtract Damage Resistance, apply wounding modifiers, and record injury.
The campaign is playable only after the GM defines point budget, technology, allowed traits, supernatural systems, and realism options.
minimum_materials: A Game Master and one or more players.
At least three ordinary six-sided dice; several sets are convenient.
Character sheets or another way to record traits, equipment, HP, and FP.
A defined campaign premise and character-building limits.
GURPS Lite for a free introductory game, or the Fourth Edition Basic Set for the complete core rules.
recommended_learning_path: Use pre-generated characters or one of this file's onboarding archetypes.
Learn success rolls, margins, contests, and active defenses.
Run basic combat without optional hit locations or harsh injury.
Add campaign-specific social, equipment, magic, power, or tactical detail only after the core loop is comfortable.

preparation: Use a focused premise and pre-generated or template-based characters.
Put each character's three most-used skills, attack, damage, defenses, HP, and FP in a visible quick-reference box.
Choose basic combat and at most one optional rule layer.

teaches: A simple Perception or reaction roll
A Quick Contest such as Stealth versus Perception or Influence versus resistance

game_master: Define campaign limits before character creation.
Select which optional rules and supplements are active.
Set fair modifiers based on circumstances.
Control non-player characters and the world.
Avoid making every scene a roll or every problem a combat.
players: Describe goals and methods rather than merely naming skills.
Know the character's most-used skills, defenses, damage, HP, FP, and disadvantages.
Help maintain the agreed campaign tone.

core_loop.name: Describe
core_loop.procedure: The GM establishes the situation, immediate sensory information, time pressure, and obvious choices.

core_loop.name: Declare intent and method
core_loop.procedure: A player states what the character wants and how the character attempts it.

core_loop.name: Select resolution
core_loop.procedure: The GM decides whether the result is automatic, impossible, a success roll, a contest, a reaction roll, damage, or another subsystem.

core_loop.name: Set effective value
core_loop.procedure: Choose the controlling attribute, skill, defense, or other value and apply all relevant modifiers.

core_loop.name: Roll and compare
core_loop.procedure: Roll 3d6 low for most success and defense rolls; use damage dice, reaction rolls, or special procedures where applicable.

core_loop.name: Apply margin and consequences
core_loop.procedure: Determine success, failure, critical result, margin, injury, resource change, or fictional consequence.

core_loop.name: Update the situation
core_loop.procedure: Record HP, FP, ammunition, conditions, relationships, time, and new choices, then repeat.

table_roles_and_core_loop.central_principle: Do not roll for routine actions with no meaningful uncertainty or consequence. Roll when the outcome matters.

session_zero_and_campaign_configuration.why_it_matters: GURPS is a toolkit. A campaign becomes playable when the Game Master narrows the toolkit to a specific genre, power level, technology level, realism level, and approved set of traits.

session_zero_checklist.question: Who are the heroes, what do they do, and why do they stay together?
Is this realistic, cinematic, horrific, heroic, comedic, gritty, or mixed?
What technology exists, and what equipment is normally available?
Do magic, psionics, divine powers, superscience, or superhuman abilities exist?
How many character points build a starting hero?
How many points may come from disadvantages and reduced attributes?
Which advantages, disadvantages, skills, powers, and templates are approved, restricted, or forbidden?
Will the game use basic combat, tactical maps, hit locations, bleeding, harsh injury, cinematic options, or a selected subset?
How much emphasis is placed on reaction rolls, Influence skills, research, mysteries, status, wealth, and organizations?
Which themes are welcome, should remain off-screen, or are excluded?

suggested_starting_point_ranges.note: The GM should tightly control severe disadvantages and niche competence.
A common range for capable but still human-scale protagonists.
Requires clearer niche protection and stronger campaign limits.
Use templates, power frameworks, and careful GM review.

session_zero_and_campaign_configuration.range_note: These are practical orientation ranges, not mandatory official tiers. The Game Master sets the actual budget.

dice_and_notation.primary_roll: 3d6 means roll three ordinary six-sided dice and add them.
dice_and_notation.roll_low: Success rolls, resistance rolls, self-control rolls, and active defenses normally succeed by rolling at or below the target number, subject to automatic-result rules.
dice_and_notation.roll_high: Damage and reaction rolls generally benefit from higher totals.

damage_notation_examples.meaning: Roll two six-sided dice, total them, then add 1.
Roll one six-sided die and subtract 2, applying any minimum-damage rule.
Roll three six-sided dice, total them, then multiply by 2 when the specific rule uses this notation.

dice_and_notation.margin: Margin of success equals effective target minus roll; margin of failure equals roll minus effective target.

character_creation.overview: Build the person the campaign needs by spending a fixed character-point budget. Costs are positive for beneficial traits and negative for disadvantages or reduced capabilities.
recommended_order: Write a one-sentence concept and party role.
Confirm the campaign point budget, disadvantage limit, and allowed sources.
Set the four basic attributes.
Adjust secondary characteristics only when the concept needs them.
Choose social background, languages, cultural familiarity, wealth, status, and technology familiarity.
Choose advantages and perks that define exceptional capabilities.
Choose disadvantages and quirks that will genuinely appear in play.
Buy the skills the character uses professionally and under pressure.
Select equipment and calculate encumbrance, defenses, and damage.
Audit the sheet for legal costs, campaign fit, and obvious capability gaps.

basic_attributes.name: Intelligence
governs: Most mental, social, technical, and magical skills

basic_attributes.name: Health
governs: Resistance to unconsciousness, death, disease, and poison

design_advice: Attributes affect many skills and should represent broad capability.
A narrow specialist often saves points by buying individual skills instead of raising a whole attribute.
Extreme attribute values should require GM approval because they reshape many subsystems.

entries.name: Hit Points
entries.meaning: Capacity to withstand injury before unconsciousness, death checks, and destruction thresholds.

entries.name: Will
entries.meaning: Mental resistance, self-control in some situations, and concentration under pressure.

entries.name: Perception
entries.meaning: Noticing hidden, distant, or subtle things.

entries.name: Fatigue Points
entries.meaning: Energy expended by exertion, extra effort, powers, deprivation, and some attacks.
Turn order, Dodge, and general quickness.
Ground movement in yards per one-second combat turn before encumbrance and other modifiers.

advantages.definition: Beneficial innate, learned, social, supernatural, or cinematic capabilities purchased with points.
examples_by_function: Social rank, reputation, contacts, or wealth
controls: Exotic and supernatural traits should exist only when the campaign permits them.
Enhancements can increase an advantage's cost and capability.
Limitations can reduce cost by imposing meaningful restrictions.

perks.definition: Small advantages that normally cost 1 point.

disadvantages.definition: Meaningful limitations that return points and must affect play.
controls: The Game Master sets a disadvantage limit.
A disadvantage that never matters is not a legitimate source of points.
Conflicting, disruptive, or campaign-breaking disadvantages may be forbidden.
Some mental disadvantages use a self-control roll when a character tries to resist.

quirks.definition: Minor personality traits or inconveniences, commonly worth -1 point each.

skills.definition: Learned capabilities based on an attribute and a difficulty category.

standard_point_progression.note: The exact starting level depends on difficulty and controlling attribute.
typical_pattern: 2 points raises it by one level from the 1-point level.
4 points raises it by one more level.
Each additional +1 usually costs 4 more points.

defaults.definition: Some skills may be attempted untrained from an attribute or related skill at a penalty.
limits: Not every skill has a default.
A default is not the same as owning the skill.
Training or familiarity requirements can still prevent an attempt.
Buying at least 1 point normally replaces reliance on the default.

specializations_and_familiarity: Some skills require a specific specialty.
Using unfamiliar equipment, culture, procedures, or models can impose penalties until familiarity is gained.
The GM should identify campaign-critical specialties before play.
skill_selection_advice: Buy the skills the character must use during danger, not only background hobbies.
Every adventurer benefits from perception, movement, communication, and survival-related competence appropriate to the setting.
Avoid spending most points on a single spectacular ability while leaving the character unable to participate in ordinary scenes.
Templates reduce analysis paralysis and protect party roles.

templates_and_lenses.template: A packaged set of required and optional traits representing an occupation, species, archetype, or role.
templates_and_lenses.lens: A smaller package layered onto a template to represent a subtype, specialty, origin, or variation.
templates_and_lenses.best_use: The GM can present approved templates and lenses so players choose among campaign-appropriate options without searching the entire rule library.

topics: Patrons, Allies, Contacts, Enemies, Dependents, and Duties
social_and_setting_traits.advice: These traits matter most when the campaign uses them consistently. The GM should explain which societies, organizations, and resource levels are important.

final_sheet_audit: Point total equals the campaign budget.
Disadvantages remain within the allowed limit.
All exotic, supernatural, cinematic, and social traits are approved.
Skill specialties and prerequisites are legal.
Equipment matches technology, wealth, legality, and availability.
The character can contribute to the party's main activity.
The character has a reason to cooperate with the other protagonists.

procedure: Choose the relevant attribute or skill.
Apply bonuses and penalties to produce effective skill.
Roll 3d6.
A result less than or equal to effective skill succeeds unless an automatic-failure rule applies.
A result above effective skill fails.
The difference is the margin of success or margin of failure.
success_roll.probability_note: Because 3d6 produces a bell curve, a one-point modifier near ordinary skill levels matters more than it would on a flat d20 roll.

critical_success: A natural 3 or 4 is always a critical success.
A natural 5 is a critical success when effective skill is at least 15.
A natural 6 is a critical success when effective skill is at least 16.
critical_failure: A natural 18 is always a critical failure.
A natural 17 is a critical failure when effective skill is 15 or less.
Any roll at least 10 greater than effective skill is a critical failure.
automatic_and_critical_results.note: The official rules contain specific critical-result tables and situation-dependent effects that are not reproduced here.

modifiers.principle: Use the character's effective chance under the actual circumstances, not the unmodified sheet number.
common_sources: Visibility, noise, range, speed, posture, or footing
Injury, fatigue, shock, distraction, or unfamiliarity
Assistance, preparation, research, or favorable conditions

task_difficulty.principle: The sheet value describes trained capability; the effective value describes this attempt under actual conditions.
task_difficulty.avoid_double_counting: Do not apply two modifiers for the same fictional obstacle unless separate rules clearly require both.

complementary_skills.rule_status: core rule highlighted in later printings and the revised Basic Set
complementary_skills.summary: One skill can sometimes assist another task, granting a modest bonus or penalty based on the supporting roll.
gm_check: do not chain unlimited complementary rolls
decide who makes the primary roll

time_spent.summary: Extra time can improve many noncombat tasks; rushing can penalize them. Exact limits depend on task and rule.
time_spent.not_for: Actions whose timing is fixed by combat, emergencies, or a specific subsystem unless that rule permits it.

quick_contest.use_when: Two capabilities oppose each other and the result can be decided in one exchange.
procedure: Each side makes the appropriate success roll.
Compare margins of success; a successful roll beats a failed roll.
The greater margin wins.
Resolve ties according to the situation or repeat if the rules call for it.
examples: A social Influence attempt versus resistance

regular_contest.use_when: Opposition continues over time and repeated effort matters.
regular_contest.procedure: Both sides roll repeatedly under the relevant rules until one side achieves the required decisive result.

reaction_rolls.purpose: Determine an NPC's initial attitude or a group's response when it is not predetermined.
procedure: Roll 3d6.
Unlike success rolls, higher is better.
Apply reaction modifiers from appearance, reputation, status, behavior, circumstances, and relevant traits.
Consult the official reaction table for the response category.
reaction_rolls.important_distinction: A reaction roll is not the same as an Influence skill roll. Influence skills are deliberate attempts to change or secure an NPC response.

influence_rolls.summary: Use an appropriate social skill and the resistance procedure specified by the skill and situation. Success can produce a defined favorable response; failure can worsen the situation.
influence_rolls.advice: Roleplay the approach first, then roll when uncertainty remains. A strong speech does not excuse a missing capability, and a high skill does not force an NPC to violate impossible boundaries.

procedure: A disadvantage specifies or permits a self-control number.
When resistance is allowed, roll 3d6 at or below that number.
Success resists the behavior for that situation; failure means portray the disadvantage's effect.
The selected number modifies the disadvantage's point value.
self_control_rolls.note: Some disadvantages do not use self-control rolls or have special triggers.

core_mechanics.fright_checks: A frightening event may require a Will-based Fright Check with modifiers. Failure uses the official Fright Check procedure and table.

resistance_rolls.summary: Hazards and abilities frequently call for HT, Will, or another attribute roll, sometimes with a penalty based on effect strength.
resistance_rolls.margin_use: Duration or severity may depend on margin of failure or success.
resistance_rolls.rule_priority: Use the specific ability, poison, disease, spell, or hazard text over general procedure.

procedure: Roleplay the request, leverage, threat, negotiation, or deception.
Determine what the NPC wants, fears, knows, and can legally or morally do.
Choose a reaction roll, Influence roll, contest, or automatic result.
Apply social traits, status, reputation, appearance, culture, language, and circumstances.
Translate the result into a believable response rather than mind control.

influence_skills.Diplomacy: Honest negotiation and broad social problem-solving with safer failure behavior.
influence_skills.Fast-Talk: Short-term deception, pressure, or rapid persuasion.
influence_skills.Intimidation: Cooperation through fear, threats, or demonstrated dominance.
influence_skills.Savoir-Faire: Correct behavior and influence within a defined social sphere.
influence_skills.Sex Appeal: Influence through physical presence and flirtation where appropriate.
influence_skills.Streetwise: Influence and information within street or criminal culture.

limits: An NPC cannot grant authority, knowledge, or resources they do not possess.
Success should change plausible behavior within motives and constraints.

summary: Basic Move measures unencumbered ground speed in combat.
Carried weight produces encumbrance levels based on Basic Lift.
Terrain, posture, injury, fatigue, and movement mode further modify travel.

travel_and_time.summary: Outside combat, resolve movement at an appropriate time scale: seconds, minutes, hours, days, or longer. Use rolls only for hazards, navigation, pursuit, fatigue, or meaningful uncertainty.

stealth.summary: Stealth is usually opposed by Perception in a Quick Contest, modified for movement, cover, noise, light, distance, alertness, and equipment.

hazards.note: The Basic Set provides detailed procedures; the GM should use only hazards relevant to the campaign.

healing.natural_recovery: Under ordinary conditions, a daily HT roll can restore HP; traits, medical care, magic, technology, and campaign realism modify recovery.
healing.first_aid: First Aid can stabilize and restore limited HP according to technology level, time, and the official treatment rules.
healing.long_term_care: Physician skill, surgery, hospitalization, magical healing, regeneration, and advanced technology use their own procedures.

advice: The GM defines which equipment lists are available.
Starting wealth does not guarantee access to restricted or setting-inappropriate items.
Record ammunition, power cells, consumables, and carried weight when they matter.

technology_level.summary: Technology Level categorizes a society's general technological development. Characters can be familiar with a home TL and may suffer penalties or require skills when using unfamiliar technology.
technology_level.campaign_use: Set a baseline TL and identify superscience, anachronisms, restricted gear, and cross-TL access.

scale_and_sequence.distance_unit: One yard per map hex in the standard tactical scale
turn_order: Act from highest Basic Speed to lowest.
Use DX and then the prescribed tie procedure when Basic Speed is tied.
The order normally remains fixed through the combat.

turn_procedure: At the start of the turn, choose a maneuver.
Perform the movement, attack, defense setup, readying, concentration, or other action allowed by that maneuver.
Active defenses usually occur during enemies' turns and depend on the maneuver already chosen.
Track shock, stun, posture, aim, readiness, ammunition, FP, HP, and ongoing effects.

maneuvers.name: Do Nothing
maneuvers.active_defenses: normal unless stunned or another condition changes them
maneuvers.summary: Take no deliberate action; commonly required while mentally stunned.

maneuvers.name: Move
maneuvers.summary: Concentrate on movement without a normal attack.

maneuvers.name: Change Posture
maneuvers.movement: posture change rather than ordinary movement
maneuvers.summary: Stand, sit, kneel, crouch, crawl, or lie down as permitted.

maneuvers.name: Aim
maneuvers.movement: step or none depending on circumstances
maneuvers.active_defenses: normal, but a defense can spoil Aim
maneuvers.summary: Prepare a ranged attack to claim Accuracy and later aiming benefits.

maneuvers.name: Evaluate
maneuvers.summary: Study one melee opponent to improve a later attack, normally up to a limited cumulative bonus.

maneuvers.name: Attack
maneuvers.summary: Make one ordinary attack or another action defined as an Attack maneuver.

maneuvers.name: Feint
maneuvers.summary: Use a combat-skill contest to reduce the target's defense against a later attack.

maneuvers.name: All-Out Attack
maneuvers.summary: Trade all active defenses for an offensive option such as greater accuracy, damage, or multiple attacks.

maneuvers.name: All-Out Defense
maneuvers.summary: Devote the turn to survival through an increased defense or a second defense against one attack.

maneuvers.name: Move and Attack
maneuvers.summary: Combine substantial movement with an attack under strict accuracy limits.

maneuvers.name: Ready
maneuvers.summary: Draw, reload, change grip, switch an item on, or otherwise prepare equipment.

maneuvers.name: Concentrate
maneuvers.active_defenses: normal, but interruption can spoil concentration
maneuvers.summary: Perform a sustained mental action, spell, or power activation.

maneuvers.name: Wait
maneuvers.active_defenses: normal until trigger; then follow the chosen maneuver
maneuvers.summary: Declare a perceivable trigger and act when it occurs.

steps: Choose target, attack type, weapon, maneuver, and any options such as hit location or Deceptive Attack.
Calculate effective attack skill after all modifiers.
On failure, the attack misses unless a special rule says otherwise.
On success, the defender may attempt one legal active defense unless denied by surprise, maneuver, condition, or special effect.
If the defense succeeds, the attack is avoided or stopped.
If the defense fails, roll damage.
Apply armor divisor, Damage Resistance, penetrating damage, damage type, hit location, and other injury modifiers.
Apply shock, knockdown, stun, crippling, unconsciousness, death checks, and other consequences as required.

types.name: Dodge
types.base_formula: Basic Speed + 3, dropping fractions, then modified by encumbrance and circumstances

types.name: Parry
types.base_formula: Half the relevant weapon or unarmed combat skill, dropping fractions, + 3
types.use: Deflect or stop an attack with a weapon or limb.

types.name: Block
types.use: Stop an attack with a shield or suitable blocking object.

retreat.summary: A defender may often step away from an attacker to improve one active defense.
typical_bonus: +1 to most other Parries or Blocks
retreat.limits: Retreat requires legal movement and is limited by position, posture, terrain, and the number of retreats allowed.

restrictions: Stun, posture, encumbrance, visibility, surprise, and attack type can modify or prevent defenses.
Dodge can normally be attempted repeatedly; Block and repeated Parries have tighter limits or penalties.
Some attacks cannot be parried or blocked safely.

attack_options.name: Deceptive Attack
attack_options.summary: Voluntarily reduce attack skill by 2 for each -1 imposed on the defender's active defense.

attack_options.name: Rapid Strike
attack_options.summary: Make multiple attacks by accepting a large skill penalty; cinematic training can reduce that penalty.

attack_options.name: Targeted Hit Location
attack_options.summary: Accept a location penalty to attack a specific body part with different injury or crippling effects.

attack_options.name: Wild Swing
attack_options.summary: Attack a target that cannot be seen clearly using the special cap and restrictions.

attack_options.name: Slam
attack_options.summary: Collide with a target using movement and mass to determine results.

attack_options.name: Grapple
attack_options.summary: Seize a target to restrict movement and enable follow-up grappling actions.

attack_options.name: Takedown
attack_options.summary: Bring a grappled opponent to the ground through a contest.

attack_options.name: Pin
attack_options.summary: Immobilize an opponent already on the ground and grappled.

attack_options.name: Disarm
attack_options.summary: Attack or contest an opponent's weapon to force it from their control.

attack_options.name: Feint
attack_options.summary: Win a contest to penalize the target's defense against a later attack.

attack_options.name: Dual-Weapon Attack
attack_options.summary: Attack with two weapons under off-hand and coordination penalties unless trained.

attack_options.name: All-Out Attack (Determined)
attack_options.summary: Gain an attack bonus while giving up all active defenses.

attack_options.name: All-Out Attack (Strong)
attack_options.summary: Increase melee damage while giving up all active defenses.

attack_options.name: All-Out Attack (Double)
attack_options.summary: Make two eligible attacks while giving up all active defenses.

attack_options.name: All-Out Attack (Feint)
attack_options.summary: Combine a Feint and attack while giving up all active defenses.

attack_options.name: Telegraphic Attack
attack_options.summary: Gain a large attack bonus but grant the defender a defense bonus because the attack is obvious.

attack_options.name: Committed Attack
attack_options.summary: Trade some defensive freedom for a smaller offensive benefit than All-Out Attack.

attack_options.name: Defensive Attack
attack_options.summary: Reduce offensive effectiveness to improve later defense.

attack_options.name: Mighty Blow
attack_options.summary: Spend FP to improve damage for one attack, subject to campaign use of extra effort in combat.

attack_options.name: Flurry of Blows
attack_options.summary: Spend FP to reduce the penalty for a Rapid Strike, subject to campaign rules.

attack_options.name: Feverish Defense
attack_options.summary: Spend FP for a one-time active-defense bonus.

attack_options.name: Suppression Fire
attack_options.summary: Fire through an area to threaten anyone entering or exposed within it.

attack_options.name: Rapid Fire
attack_options.summary: Use Rate of Fire and Recoil to determine possible multiple hits from a burst.

attack_options.name: Multiple Projectiles
attack_options.summary: Resolve attacks that launch many pellets or projectiles using their special close- and long-range behavior.

attack_options.name: Opportunity Fire
attack_options.summary: Watch an area and attack a qualifying target that appears.

melee.deceptive_attack: For every -2 voluntarily taken to melee attack skill, reduce the target's active defense by 1.

hit_locations.summary: Targeting a specific body part imposes an attack penalty and can change injury, knockdown, crippling, or armor coverage.

rapid_strike.summary: Trade a significant skill penalty for multiple melee attacks; cinematic traits can reduce the penalty.

grappling.summary: A successful grapple limits movement and enables follow-up actions such as takedowns, pins, locks, or attempts to break free.

aim: A successful later attack can receive the weapon's Accuracy after sufficient Aim.
Additional aim time, bracing, scopes, sights, and equipment can add further bonuses under their rules.
Movement, injury, losing sight of the target, or interruption can spoil Aim.
common_modifiers: Rate of Fire and aiming aids

rapid_fire.summary: A successful burst scores one hit, plus additional hits for each full multiple of the weapon's Recoil by which the attack succeeds, up to the number of shots fired and subject to the exact rapid-fire rules.
rapid_fire.required_reference: Use the official Rate of Fire, Recoil, and Rapid Fire rules for exact bonuses and limits.

ranged.range_table_note: The full Size and Speed/Range Table is intentionally not reproduced in this guide.

damage_process: Roll the attack's listed damage dice and modifiers.
Modify Damage Resistance for any armor divisor.
Subtract effective DR from basic damage.
Multiply penetrating damage by the damage type's wounding modifier and any hit-location modifier.
Round as directed by the rules to determine injury.
Subtract injury from HP and apply secondary effects.

common_wounding_modifiers.damage_type: Burning, corrosion, crushing, piercing, or toxic

secondary_effects.name: Shock
secondary_effects.summary: Recent injury can penalize DX- and IQ-based actions on the victim's next turn, normally to a maximum penalty of -4.

secondary_effects.name: Major Wound
secondary_effects.summary: A single injury greater than half the victim's HP can require a HT roll to avoid knockdown and stunning.

secondary_effects.name: Crippling Injury
secondary_effects.summary: Sufficient injury to a limb or extremity can disable it under the hit-location rules.

secondary_effects.name: Knockback
secondary_effects.summary: Some attacks can push a target based on damage and ST.

secondary_effects.name: Bleeding
secondary_effects.summary: Certain wounds can continue causing harm until treated.

hp_thresholds.effect: Basic Move and Dodge are reduced.
Roll HT at the start of each turn to remain conscious, subject to the full rules.

hp_thresholds.threshold: Each further full negative multiple of HP

hp_thresholds.effect: Usually represents total bodily destruction when the damage source can cause it.

fatigue.summary: FP represent short-term energy. Exertion, deprivation, heat, powers, extra effort, and some attacks reduce FP.
fatigue.low_fp: At very low FP, physical performance falls sharply. At 0 FP, additional exertion can cause HP loss and other consequences under the full rules.
fatigue.recovery: Rest normally restores FP, with the rate affected by conditions, traits, and the source of fatigue.

surprise_and_stun.surprise: A surprised character may be mentally stunned and unable to act effectively until recovery.
surprise_and_stun.mental_stun: A mentally stunned character normally must Do Nothing and make an IQ roll on later turns to recover.
surprise_and_stun.physical_stun: A physically stunned character has reduced defenses, may fall, and rolls HT to recover.

conditions_and_states.name: Mental Stun
core_effects: Usually must Do Nothing.
Active defenses are penalized.
Roll IQ on later turns to recover.
conditions_and_states.clearance: Successful recovery roll or other rule.

conditions_and_states.name: Physical Stun
core_effects: May fall down.
Active defenses are penalized.
Cannot act normally until recovery.
conditions_and_states.clearance: Roll HT on later turns to recover.

conditions_and_states.name: Unconscious
core_effects: Cannot act or defend normally.
May be vulnerable to further injury.
conditions_and_states.clearance: Recovery depends on cause, HP, HT, treatment, and special rules.

conditions_and_states.name: Shock
core_effects: Recent injury penalizes many DX- and IQ-based actions on the next turn.
The ordinary cap is -4.
conditions_and_states.clearance: Normally ends after the victim's next turn.

conditions_and_states.name: Major Wound
core_effects: A sufficiently large single injury can trigger knockdown and stunning.
Some damage types and locations use special thresholds.
conditions_and_states.clearance: Resolve the immediate HT roll and any resulting stun or knockdown.

conditions_and_states.name: Crippled Limb or Extremity
core_effects: The body part cannot be used normally.
Duration may be temporary, lasting, or permanent depending on injury and recovery.
conditions_and_states.clearance: Healing and the official crippling-injury rules.

conditions_and_states.name: Prone
core_effects: Movement and attacks are restricted.
Ranged profile and melee defenses change.

damage_pipeline: Roll the attack's listed damage dice and modifiers.
Modify Damage Resistance for any armor divisor.
Subtract effective DR from basic damage.
Multiply penetrating damage by the damage type's wounding modifier and any hit-location modifier.
Round as directed by the rules to determine injury.
Subtract injury from HP and apply secondary effects.

armor_divisors.procedure: Modify DR before subtracting it from basic damage.
armor_divisors.rounding: Use the official rule for rounding effective DR.

hazards.note: The Basic Set provides detailed procedures; the GM should use only hazards relevant to the campaign.

magic_powers_and_special_systems.core_principle: GURPS does not require one universal supernatural system. The Game Master selects a model that fits the setting.

approaches.name: Skill-based magic
approaches.summary: Spells are learned as skills, influenced by mana and prerequisites. The Basic Set introduces the framework; GURPS Magic greatly expands it.

approaches.name: Advantages as powers
approaches.summary: Build abilities from advantages, enhancements, limitations, power modifiers, and related skills. GURPS Powers expands this approach.

approaches.name: Psionics
approaches.summary: Commonly built as powers with abilities grouped by source and focus; specialized supplements add detail.

approaches.name: Divine or spirit abilities
approaches.summary: Can be represented by powers, granted advantages, learned rituals, reaction-based aid, or another approved subsystem.

approaches.name: Alternative magic systems
approaches.summary: GURPS supports many alternatives, including ritual, path, realm, syntactic, improvisational, and setting-specific systems.

power_design_workflow: Describe the fictional effect without mechanics.
Choose the closest advantage or other base trait.
Apply enhancements for broader or stronger capability.
Apply limitations for meaningful restrictions; ordinary limitation total is capped by the core rules.
Choose a power source and power modifier if the campaign uses them.
Choose the controlling attribute, activation roll, resistance, duration, and resource cost.
Define counters, detection, special effects, and interaction with other powers.
Compare with existing party capabilities and revise before play.
magic_powers_and_special_systems.important_warning: The core book introduces magic but does not contain the full GURPS Magic spell catalog. This JSON does not reproduce proprietary spell descriptions.

spending_options: Learn new skills when training or experience justifies them.
Raise attributes or secondary characteristics with GM approval.
Buy new advantages when the story explains their acquisition.
Buy off disadvantages when play justifies the change.
Acquire social traits, contacts, rank, wealth, or powers through events.
advancement_and_training.training_and_justification: The GM decides whether points alone are sufficient or whether instruction, time, access, transformation, or an in-world event is required.
advancement_and_training.no_character_levels: GURPS has no mandatory class level. Growth is purchased directly in the traits that improve.

before_the_campaign: Set point totals and disadvantage limits.
Define technology, supernatural assumptions, and available gear.
Create an allowed-trait list or templates.
Select only the optional rules that support the intended experience.
Prepare a brief explanation of what competent characters should be able to do.
before_each_session: Review character disadvantages, duties, enemies, allies, and unresolved goals.
Prepare situations rather than a single mandatory plot path.
Record likely NPC motives and only the statistics that may be used.
Identify terrain, clues, resources, and consequences.
Have ordinary task modifiers and combat statistics ready.
during_play: State the stakes before an important roll when possible.
Use one roll to answer one meaningful question.
Prefer broad rulings over stopping play to search for an obscure modifier.
Record temporary rulings and verify them after the session.
Use reaction and morale rather than assuming every NPC fights irrationally.
Call for disadvantages when they matter, but do not use them solely to punish players.
after_play: Update relationships, resources, injuries, reputation, and campaign clocks.
Ask which rules added fun and which added friction.
Add or remove optional detail deliberately.

npc_design.principle: Most NPCs do not need complete point accounting.
minimum_stat_block: DR, HP, and FP when relevant

preparation: Use a focused premise and pre-generated or template-based characters.
Put each character's three most-used skills, attack, damage, defenses, HP, and FP in a visible quick-reference box.
Choose basic combat and at most one optional rule layer.

worked_examples.name: Ordinary success roll
worked_examples.setup: A character has Climbing-12. Rain and poor handholds impose -2.
worked_examples.result: Success by 2. The character climbs successfully with a margin of success of 2.

worked_examples.name: Failed success roll
worked_examples.setup: A character has Electronics Repair-11 and attempts a rushed repair at -3.
worked_examples.result: Failure by 4. The GM applies a consequence such as lost time, worsened damage, or the need for better tools.

worked_examples.name: Quick Contest
worked_examples.setup: An infiltrator rolls Stealth-13 against a guard's Perception-12.
worked_examples.result: The infiltrator wins the Quick Contest by 2 and remains unnoticed under the circumstances.

worked_examples.name: Basic melee attack
worked_examples.setup: A fighter has Broadsword-14 and takes -2 in situational penalties.
worked_examples.defense: The target has Dodge-9; roll 11, failure.
worked_examples.damage: The attack rolls 7 cutting damage. The target has DR 3, leaving 4 penetrating damage. Cutting's ×1.5 wounding modifier produces 6 injury.
worked_examples.result: The target loses 6 HP and may suffer shock or other effects depending on total HP and circumstances.

worked_examples.name: Deceptive Attack
worked_examples.setup: A duelist with Rapier-16 voluntarily takes -4 to attack.
worked_examples.calculation: Attack is made at effective skill 12, and the defender suffers -2 to the chosen active defense if the attack succeeds.
worked_examples.result: This trades accuracy for a better chance of getting past a skilled defense.

worked_examples.name: Reaction versus Influence
worked_examples.setup: The heroes approach a neutral official.
worked_examples.reaction_use: If the official's starting attitude is uncertain, the GM can make a reaction roll.
worked_examples.influence_use: If a hero then makes a specific request using Diplomacy, Fast-Talk, Intimidation, or another appropriate skill, resolve that deliberate attempt under the Influence rules.
worked_examples.result: Initial attitude and deliberate persuasion are related but distinct procedures.

worked_examples.name: Encumbrance and Dodge
worked_examples.setup: A ST 10 character has Basic Lift 20 lb, Basic Move 5, and unencumbered Dodge 8. The character carries 45 lb.
worked_examples.calculation: 45 lb is above 2×BL but no more than 3×BL, so this is Medium encumbrance. Apply the Medium movement multiplier and -2 Dodge.
worked_examples.result: Move becomes 3 after the ordinary multiplier and rounding procedure; Dodge becomes 6 before other modifiers.

worked_examples.name: Skill purchase
worked_examples.setup: A character with DX 12 buys an Average DX skill.
worked_examples.calculation: 1 point gives DX-1, 2 points gives DX, 4 points gives DX+1, and each further +1 costs 4 points.

worked_examples.name: Self-control value
worked_examples.setup: A disadvantage has a listed base value and the player selects a self-control number of 9.
worked_examples.calculation: The standard multiplier for 9 or less is ×1.5.
worked_examples.result: Apply the multiplier to the disadvantage's base negative value and use the official rounding rule.

worked_examples.name: Enhancements and limitations
worked_examples.setup: A 20-point advantage has +50% in enhancements and -30% in limitations.
worked_examples.result: Final cost is 24 points unless the trait has a special costing rule.

common_mistakes.mistake: Trying to use every GURPS rule.
common_mistakes.correction: Choose the smallest rule set that supports the campaign, then add detail only when it improves play.

common_mistakes.mistake: Allowing players to search every published trait without campaign limits.
common_mistakes.correction: Use an approved list, templates, or GM-reviewed proposals.

common_mistakes.mistake: Confusing roll-low and roll-high mechanics.
common_mistakes.correction: Success rolls and defenses usually want low results; damage and reaction rolls generally want high results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Building characters independently before the campaign is defined.
common_mistakes.correction: Set premise, points, technology, powers, and roles first.

common_mistakes.mistake: Treating disadvantages as free points.
common_mistakes.correction: Disadvantages must appear in play and shape decisions.

common_mistakes.mistake: Ignoring active defenses.
common_mistakes.correction: A successful attack roll normally gives the target a separate defense roll.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using point total as the only measure of combat difficulty.
common_mistakes.correction: Equipment, skill concentration, defenses, mobility, terrain, surprise, objectives, and action economy dominate many encounters.

common_mistakes.mistake: Making every failed information roll stop the adventure.
common_mistakes.correction: Use costs, delays, partial clues, risk, or alternate paths instead of dead ends.

common_mistakes.mistake: Letting optional realism surprise the players.
common_mistakes.correction: Declare harsh injury, bleeding, ammunition, encumbrance, survival, and social-detail rules before play.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using the unmodified skill from the sheet as the final target.
common_mistakes.correction: Always calculate effective skill for the actual circumstances.

common_mistakes.mistake: Buying a broad attribute when only one narrow skill needs improvement, or buying many narrow skills when a broad attribute would be cheaper.
common_mistakes.correction: Compare total point cost and concept before finalizing.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming every advantage, spell, cinematic skill, or technology exists in every campaign.
common_mistakes.correction: Treat the GM's campaign configuration as an allowlist.

common_mistakes.mistake: Failing to record encumbrance and current Dodge.
common_mistakes.correction: Calculate carried weight before play and update it when major gear changes.

common_mistakes.mistake: Treating one-second turns as a universal round clock.
common_mistakes.correction: Each combatant's next turn occurs about one second after that combatant's previous turn; defensive consequences can persist until then.

trait_modifier_engine.rounding: Round final positive point costs according to the official rule, normally upward to the next whole point.
exceptions: some advantages use special modifier rules
some limitations modify only part of a trait
alternative abilities and power frameworks use additional rules

self_control_engine.validation: Only traits that permit a self-control number use this engine.

encumbrance_engine.over_extra_heavy: Ordinary characters cannot move normally while carrying more than 10 × Basic Lift without a special rule.
encumbrance_engine.rounding: Drop fractions from modified Move unless a specific rule says otherwise.

critical_failure: any result at least 10 above effective skill

success_probability_engine.probability_cap_note: Because 17 and 18 always fail, ordinary success chance does not exceed 98.1481% regardless of very high effective skill.

combat_engine.turn_order_formula: descending Basic Speed; use the official tie procedure
attack_pipeline: if successful, allow legal active defense
if defense fails, roll basic damage

corrosion.additional_note: Can reduce DR under its specific rules.

wealth_engine.currency_note: GURPS uses campaign dollars as an abstract comparison unit; the GM defines actual currency and purchasing context.
wealth_engine.access_note: Wealth does not override legality, availability, Status, Rank, or setting restrictions.

technology_engine.split_tl: A setting can have different TLs by field or society.

builder_validation_rules.rule: point total must equal campaign budget plus earned points unless GM permits unspent points
negative points from disadvantages and reduced traits must respect the campaign limit and counting policy
exotic, supernatural, cinematic, social, and setting-sensitive traits require campaign permission
skills, spells, techniques, and abilities must satisfy all stated prerequisites
skills requiring a specialty must record one
equipment and skills should match campaign TL or explicitly record cross-TL access
unfamiliar models, cultures, and procedures may require penalties until familiar
carried weight must produce a current encumbrance level, Move, and Dodge
at least one attack and every commonly available active defense should be calculated
concept and disadvantages must permit participation in the campaign and party
do not buy overlapping traits twice unless the rules explicitly permit stacking
ordinary limitations cannot reduce an advantage below the core limitation cap without a special rule

do_nothing.name: Do Nothing
do_nothing.active_defenses: normal unless stunned or another condition changes them
do_nothing.summary: Take no deliberate action; commonly required while mentally stunned.

move.name: Move
move.summary: Concentrate on movement without a normal attack.

change_posture.name: Change Posture
change_posture.movement: posture change rather than ordinary movement
change_posture.summary: Stand, sit, kneel, crouch, crawl, or lie down as permitted.

aim.name: Aim
aim.movement: step or none depending on circumstances
aim.active_defenses: normal, but a defense can spoil Aim
aim.summary: Prepare a ranged attack to claim Accuracy and later aiming benefits.

evaluate.name: Evaluate
evaluate.summary: Study one melee opponent to improve a later attack, normally up to a limited cumulative bonus.

attack.name: Attack
attack.summary: Make one ordinary attack or another action defined as an Attack maneuver.

feint.name: Feint
feint.summary: Use a combat-skill contest to reduce the target's defense against a later attack.

all_out_attack.name: All-Out Attack
all_out_attack.summary: Trade all active defenses for an offensive option such as greater accuracy, damage, or multiple attacks.

all_out_defense.name: All-Out Defense
all_out_defense.summary: Devote the turn to survival through an increased defense or a second defense against one attack.

move_and_attack.name: Move and Attack
move_and_attack.summary: Combine substantial movement with an attack under strict accuracy limits.

ready.name: Ready
ready.summary: Draw, reload, change grip, switch an item on, or otherwise prepare equipment.

concentrate.name: Concentrate
concentrate.active_defenses: normal, but interruption can spoil concentration
concentrate.summary: Perform a sustained mental action, spell, or power activation.

wait.name: Wait
wait.active_defenses: normal until trigger; then follow the chosen maneuver
wait.summary: Declare a perceivable trigger and act when it occurs.

deceptive_attack.name: Deceptive Attack
deceptive_attack.summary: Voluntarily reduce attack skill by 2 for each -1 imposed on the defender's active defense.

rapid_strike.name: Rapid Strike
rapid_strike.summary: Make multiple attacks by accepting a large skill penalty; cinematic training can reduce that penalty.

targeted_attack.name: Targeted Hit Location
targeted_attack.summary: Accept a location penalty to attack a specific body part with different injury or crippling effects.

wild_swing.name: Wild Swing
wild_swing.summary: Attack a target that cannot be seen clearly using the special cap and restrictions.

slam.name: Slam
slam.summary: Collide with a target using movement and mass to determine results.

grapple.name: Grapple
grapple.summary: Seize a target to restrict movement and enable follow-up grappling actions.

takedown.name: Takedown
takedown.summary: Bring a grappled opponent to the ground through a contest.

pin.name: Pin
pin.summary: Immobilize an opponent already on the ground and grappled.

disarm.name: Disarm
disarm.summary: Attack or contest an opponent's weapon to force it from their control.

feint.name: Feint
feint.summary: Win a contest to penalize the target's defense against a later attack.

dual_weapon_attack.name: Dual-Weapon Attack
dual_weapon_attack.summary: Attack with two weapons under off-hand and coordination penalties unless trained.

all_out_attack_determined.name: All-Out Attack (Determined)
all_out_attack_determined.summary: Gain an attack bonus while giving up all active defenses.

all_out_attack_strong.name: All-Out Attack (Strong)
all_out_attack_strong.summary: Increase melee damage while giving up all active defenses.

all_out_attack_double.name: All-Out Attack (Double)
all_out_attack_double.summary: Make two eligible attacks while giving up all active defenses.

all_out_attack_feint.name: All-Out Attack (Feint)
all_out_attack_feint.summary: Combine a Feint and attack while giving up all active defenses.

telegraphic_attack.name: Telegraphic Attack
telegraphic_attack.summary: Gain a large attack bonus but grant the defender a defense bonus because the attack is obvious.

committed_attack.name: Committed Attack
committed_attack.summary: Trade some defensive freedom for a smaller offensive benefit than All-Out Attack.

defensive_attack.name: Defensive Attack
defensive_attack.summary: Reduce offensive effectiveness to improve later defense.

extra_effort_mighty_blow.name: Mighty Blow
extra_effort_mighty_blow.summary: Spend FP to improve damage for one attack, subject to campaign use of extra effort in combat.

extra_effort_flurry.name: Flurry of Blows
extra_effort_flurry.summary: Spend FP to reduce the penalty for a Rapid Strike, subject to campaign rules.

extra_effort_feverish_defense.name: Feverish Defense
extra_effort_feverish_defense.summary: Spend FP for a one-time active-defense bonus.

suppressive_fire.name: Suppression Fire
suppressive_fire.summary: Fire through an area to threaten anyone entering or exposed within it.

rapid_fire.name: Rapid Fire
rapid_fire.summary: Use Rate of Fire and Recoil to determine possible multiple hits from a burst.

shotgun_and_multiple_projectiles.name: Multiple Projectiles
shotgun_and_multiple_projectiles.summary: Resolve attacks that launch many pellets or projectiles using their special close- and long-range behavior.

opportunity_fire.name: Opportunity Fire
opportunity_fire.summary: Watch an area and attack a qualifying target that appears.

mental_stun.name: Mental Stun
core_effects: Usually must Do Nothing.
Active defenses are penalized.
Roll IQ on later turns to recover.
mental_stun.clearance: Successful recovery roll or other rule.

physical_stun.name: Physical Stun
core_effects: May fall down.
Active defenses are penalized.
Cannot act normally until recovery.
physical_stun.clearance: Roll HT on later turns to recover.

unconscious.name: Unconscious
core_effects: Cannot act or defend normally.
May be vulnerable to further injury.
unconscious.clearance: Recovery depends on cause, HP, HT, treatment, and special rules.

shock.name: Shock
core_effects: Recent injury penalizes many DX- and IQ-based actions on the next turn.
The ordinary cap is -4.
shock.clearance: Normally ends after the victim's next turn.

major_wound.name: Major Wound
core_effects: A sufficiently large single injury can trigger knockdown and stunning.
Some damage types and locations use special thresholds.
major_wound.clearance: Resolve the immediate HT roll and any resulting stun or knockdown.

crippled_limb.name: Crippled Limb or Extremity
core_effects: The body part cannot be used normally.
Duration may be temporary, lasting, or permanent depending on injury and recovery.
crippled_limb.clearance: Healing and the official crippling-injury rules.

prone.name: Prone
core_effects: Movement and attacks are restricted.
Ranged profile and melee defenses change.
Standing requires a posture change.

kneeling.name: Kneeling
core_effects: Movement and combat modifiers differ from standing.
May improve use of cover.

grappled.name: Grappled
core_effects: Movement and available actions are restricted.
Breaking free normally requires an opposed action.
grappled.clearance: Break free, release, incapacitate grappler, or special ability.

pinned.name: Pinned
core_effects: Severely immobilized after grappling on the ground.
Options are extremely limited.
pinned.clearance: Win the required contest or receive assistance.

low_hp.name: Below One-Third HP
core_effects: Basic Move and Dodge are reduced.

zero_or_negative_hp.name: 0 HP or Less
core_effects: HT rolls may be required each turn to remain conscious.
Death checks begin at negative multiples of HP.

low_fp.name: Below One-Third FP
core_effects: Movement, Dodge, and physical performance are reduced under the fatigue rules.

zero_fp.name: 0 FP or Less
core_effects: Further exertion can cost HP.
Remaining active becomes increasingly difficult.
zero_fp.clearance: Rest or another source of FP recovery.

afflicted.name: Afflicted
core_effects: Apply the specific condition, trait, or penalty named by the Affliction.
afflicted.clearance: Duration, resistance, treatment, or countermeasure defined by the ability.

fright_reaction.name: Fright Reaction
core_effects: Apply the result generated by the campaign's Fright Check rules.
fright_reaction.clearance: Varies from immediate recovery to lasting mental effects.

suffocating.name: Suffocating
core_effects: Lose FP and eventually HP under the suffocation rules.

bleeding.name: Bleeding
core_effects: Continue risking HP loss after injury when the optional bleeding rules are active.
bleeding.clearance: Successful treatment, stabilization, or natural stopping.

on_fire.name: On Fire
core_effects: Take recurring burning damage and risk spreading flame.
on_fire.clearance: Extinguish the flames using an appropriate action or environment.

poisoned_or_diseased.name: Poisoned or Diseased
core_effects: Make resistance rolls and apply periodic effects defined by the hazard.
poisoned_or_diseased.clearance: Successful resistance, completed course, antidote, treatment, or immunity.
